title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page, eq. (13)). X = U_{0,3}^{an} = P^1 \ {0,1,∞}. It carries the group 𝒢 = 𝒯_{0,3} = S_3 × Z/2: the anharmonic group together with complex conjugation. Its holomorphic part is G = S_3. The special points X^! = {2,−1,1/2; −j,−j²} are the points with nontrivial stabiliser in G. The quotient map is f(z) = (27/4)·z²(z−1)²/(z²−z+1)³, the classical λ→j map in its normalised form. It sends {0,1,∞}→0, {−1,2,1/2}→1 and {−j,−j²}={e^{±iπ/3}}→∞. The target is Y = P^1 \ {0}, with orbifold multiplicities d_Y(1)=2, d_Y(∞)=3, and residual group 𝓗 = Z/2 (complex conjugation).

What the page computes. The group π_1(Y, d_Y, Z/2Z) is the orbifold fundamental group of the (2,3,∞) sphere extended by conjugation, i.e. PGL_2(Z). Grothendieck names it \tilde π'_{0,3} = "groupes cartographiques triangulés non orientés": the non-oriented cartographic group for triangulated maps, with presentation <τ'_0,τ'_1,τ'_∞ | τ'^2, (2,3) relations>. The aim (continued on the next page) is to present this group via the equivariant fundamental group π_1(X, 𝒢; x). Its elements are pairs (γ ∈ 𝒢, l = path from x to γ^{-1}x) or similar, as defined on the previous page. This realises PGL_2(Z) explicitly as an extension of S_3×Z/2 by π_1(U_{0,3}) ≅ F_2, with explicit lifts of the three reflection generators.

Step 1: choice of base points. The base point in Y is y = −j̄ = e^{iπ/3}, viewed as the north pole, i.e. the centre of the upper triangle (0,1,∞). A base point x ∈ f^{-1}(y) is needed upstairs. Since y is not a branch value, f^{-1}(y) has 6 points.
- The real line and the circles |z|=1, |z−1|=1, Re z=1/2 cut X's sphere into the 12 triangles of the barycentric subdivision of the two triangles (0,1,∞).
- Each of the 12 maps biholomorphically onto one hemisphere of Y.
- Around −j̄ in the upper half-plane there are 6 triangles; alternate ones map to the upper hemisphere.
- So the 3 northern preimages lie in the triangles (−j̄,0,1/2), (−j̄,1,2), (−j̄,∞,−1).
- They are cyclically permuted by the order-3 rotation g: z ↦ 1/(1−z), which sends 0→1→∞ and 1/2→2→−1. The transpositions of S_3 exchange the hemispheres.
- So choosing x amounts to choosing a triangle, equivalently a segment (0,1/2), (1,2) or (∞,−1). Grothendieck picks (0,1/2).

Step 2: the generators. The three involutive generators τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞ lie over the nontrivial τ ∈ Z/2. Each is given as a pair (τ, l'_i), where l'_i is a path from y = −j̄ (north pole) to τy = −j (south pole). The paths are the arcs of 'great circles' through e^{±iπ/3} crossing the equator R at 2, −1 and 1/2 respectively. Concretely these circles are:
- |z−1|=1, which meets R in {0,2};
- |z|=1, which meets R in {−1,1};
- Re z = 1/2, which meets R in {1/2,∞}.
In each case the arc avoiding the puncture or orbifold point (0, 1, ∞ of Y) is taken. Each arc crosses the side of the triangle (0,1,∞) opposite the vertex indexing the generator, so τ'_i is the reflection in the side opposite i, matching the cartographic conventions.

On the next page these paths are lifted through f to paths λ_i from x to transformed points g_i x. This gives τ'_i as explicit elements (σ̇ τ̇, λ_i) of π_1(X,𝒢;x). They are then transported to the base point P = −j̄ of X, as an input to the 'équation des lacets' / Grothendieck–Teichmüller computations.
errors: No mathematical error. The six preimages, their distribution in alternating barycentric triangles, the transitivity of the order-3 rotation, and the choice of arcs avoiding 0, 1, ∞ in Y all check out. The 'great circles' through −j̄ and −j are |z−1|=1, |z|=1 and Re z=1/2, which cross R at 2, −1 and 1/2 as claimed.

Minor notational hazard, not an error: −j̄ denotes both the order-3 orbifold point of X and the (non-special) base point of Y. The numbers 2, −1, 1/2 likewise appear both as X's order-2 points and as crossing points on Y's equator.

ideas.what: Realising PGL_2(Z) (non-oriented triangulated cartographic group) as the equivariant/orbifold fundamental group of U_{0,3} with the S_3×Z/2 action, via the explicit degree-6 j-map. Generators are given as pairs (group element, path).
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold (equivariant) fundamental group of a transformation group; extended modular group as the (2,3,∞) reflection triangle group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rhodes (fundamental group of a transformation group, 1966); Thurston (orbifolds, late 1970s); classical modular group theory (Klein)
ideas.where_published: Cartographic groups C_2, C_2^+ and their triangulated versions as π_1 of P^1 minus 3 points with Z/2: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Choice of base point via a barycentric triangle (equivalently a segment (0,1/2)) and explicit great-circle paths from north to south pole crossing the equator at 2, −1, 1/2 to define the involutive generators.
ideas.modern_name: Explicit path / tangential-type base-point bookkeeping for the S_3-symmetric presentation of π_1(M_{0,4}) used in GT relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps for GT-related computations
ideas.where_published: Possibly parts of La Longue Marche; not this specific computation as far as known

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine base-point and path computation identifying the extended modular group with the equivariant π_1 of U_{0,3} under S_3×Z/2. It is standard material and consistent with Grothendieck's known cartographic-group framework; no new result or connection appears on this page.
